qs.q: A 65-year-old man undergoes resection of a firm sigmoid colon mass. Which microscopic finding distinguishes this invasive adenocarcinoma from severe epithelial dysplasia?
o: Cellular pleomorphism
High mitotic activity
Nuclear hyperchromasia
Basement membrane breach
qs.e: Pleomorphism, mitoses, and hyperchromasia also occur in severe dysplasia, but invasion through the basement membrane defines true malignancy. Other features alone are insufficient to confirm cancer.
qs.s: Pathology by Dr. Irungu — — Oncopathology: MCQs

qs.q: When assessing the prognosis of a patient diagnosed with colorectal adenocarcinoma, which combination of factors serves as the primary histological prognostic determinants?
o: Total length of the large bowel and diet
Depth of invasion and lymph node metastases
Tumour color and patient age at presentation
Presence of hyperplastic polyps and gender
qs.e: The key prognostic factors for colorectal adenocarcinoma are the depth of invasion (T stage) and lymph node metastases (N stage). Other clinical variables do not carry the same primary prognostic weight in staging.
qs.s: Tumours of the Gastrointestinal Tract: MCQs

qs.q: A 62-year-old man undergoes screening colonoscopy, which reveals a sessile lesion in the sigmoid colon. Histological examination shows dysplastic changes confined within the lamina propria without invasion through the muscularis mucosae. What are the two most important prognostic factors for malignant colorectal adenocarcinomas that eventually develop from such precursors?
o: Histological grade of differentiation and mucin production
Depth of invasion and presence of lymph node metastases
Presence of perineural invasion and tumor location
Total number of polyps and patient age at initial onset
qs.e: The depth of tumor invasion into the bowel wall and the presence of regional lymph node metastases are the two most crucial prognostic determinants for colorectal adenocarcinoma. While histological grade matters, depth and nodal status dictate staging and long-term survival.

qs.q: During the staging of a newly diagnosed case of colorectal adenocarcinoma, the multidisciplinary team reviews the primary histological prognostic determinants. Which combination of factors primarily determines the prognosis of this malignancy?
o: Presence of signet ring cells and extracellular mucin production
Depth of invasion and presence of lymph node metastases
Anatomic location within the proximal versus distal colon
Total number of colonic polyps and patient chronological age
qs.e: Colorectal adenocarcinoma prognosis is primarily determined by the depth of invasion (T stage) and the presence or absence of lymph node metastases (N stage). Other factors like polyp count are more relevant to familial syndromes rather than sporadic staging.

qs.q: A 19-year-old woman is diagnosed with clear cell adenocarcinoma of the upper anterior vagina. This rare malignancy is most strongly associated with which of the following prenatal exposures?
o: Prenatal folic acid antagonist exposure
Prenatal progesterone supplement exposure
Prenatal oral contraceptive exposure
Prenatal diethylstilbestrol exposure
qs.e: Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina is strongly linked to in utero exposure to diethylstilbestrol (DES). It develops in young women whose mothers took DES, leading to vaginal adenosis.
qs.s: Disorders of the Vagina and Breast: MCQs

qs.q: A 62-year-old man with a locally advanced, borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma is prescribed gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel before his planned Whipple procedure. What is the primary clinical rationale for administering this drug regimen prior to surgery?
o: To eliminate any microscopic systemic spread
To provide immediate relief of biliary pain
To shrink the tumor and improve operability
To eradicate the primary local tumor mass
qs.e: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is administered before surgery specifically to reduce tumor volume and facilitate a complete resection. Adjuvant therapy, rather than neoadjuvant, is primarily intended to target microscopic residual disease.
qs.s: Oncology: Surgery, Radiotherapy & Chemotherapy Explained: MCQs

qs.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with haematuria. Biopsy of a bladder lesion reveals adenocarcinoma. Which of the following is a known origin for this tumour type?
o: Urachal remnants
Schistosoma haematobium infection
HPV infection
Chronic catheterization
qs.e: Bladder adenocarcinoma can arise from urachal remnants or extensive intestinal metaplasia. Schistosomiasis is associated with squamous cell carcinoma, not adenocarcinoma.
qs.s: Bladder Cancer & Urothelial Neoplasms: Types, Risks, Pathogenesis: MCQs

qs.q: A 70-year-old man undergoes evaluation for a newly detected nodule in the peripheral zone of the prostate. A prostate biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma. Which of the following is a characteristic metastatic pattern for advanced stages of this malignancy?
o: Exclusive superficial inguinal spread
Lytic bone destruction
Osteoblastic bone metastases
Early hematogenous lung lesions
qs.e: Prostate adenocarcinoma characteristically metastasizes to bone where lesions are typically osteoblastic in nature. It arises most frequently in the outer or peripheral zone and can be screened using serum PSA.
qs.s: Quick Guide: Male Reproductive System Pathology, Testis, Penis: MCQs
